How much does timing belt replacement cost?

A new timing belt, installed — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$918–$1,338

Parts $315–$453 · labor $603–$885

Bay Area: $300–$900 quoted by San Francisco shops.

Why quotes run $450 to $1,300

Labor
$584–$858 nationally — 3–8 hours to reach the belt. The belt is cheap; getting to it isn't.
The kit
Belt kit with tensioner and pulleys: $300–$400. The belt alone is the smallest line on the invoice.
Water pump
Add about $100 in parts while it's apart. Skip it and you'll pay the full labor again when it fails later.
Engine layout
A Civic runs $450–$685; an Audi A4 $950–$1,300. Tight engine bays bill more hours.

What the extra money buys

Belt only
Less now

Cheaper today. False economy if the pump is original — it sits behind the same covers and fails on its own schedule.

Belt + water pump
~$100 more in parts

The standard recommendation. Same labor, one visit, no repeat teardown. Ask for it itemized, not bundled.

Bottom line: always do the pump with the belt. The $100 now saves a second $600+ labor bill later.

Common questions

When should I replace it?

Every 60,000–100,000 miles or per the manual — whichever comes first. Age matters too: rubber degrades sitting still.

What happens if it breaks?

On interference engines, pistons hit valves — that's an engine rebuild, thousands of dollars. On non-interference engines you're just stranded. Either way, don't wait.

Does my car have a belt or a chain?

Chains generally last the engine's life; belts are scheduled maintenance. The manual says which — if it lists a replacement interval, it's a belt.

How long does the job take?

3–8 hours depending on the car. It's a full-day shop visit; a DIYer should budget a weekend.

Every car prices differently.

The range above is a national average. Your price depends on the engine layout and whether the pump comes along. Take a photo of your estimate in Brightglow for a second opinion on the actual car.
